claims.text: The initial material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen vacancies can be introduced into bulk HfNbTaTiZr as a single intervention.
Oxygen vacancies in HfNbTaTiZr will produce lattice distortion.
Oxygen vacancies in HfNbTaTiZr will produce strain fluctuations.
Lattice distortion and strain fluctuations strengthen phonon scattering.
Stronger phonon scattering from lattice distortion and strain fluctuations reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
Introducing oxygen vacancies will lower the lattice thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies from approximately 0 to 200 K.
The prediction is restricted to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing oxygen vacancies.
The effect of oxygen vacancies on electronic thermal conductivity is uncertain.
Interactions between oxygen vacancies and other defects may affect the result.
Thermal-conductivity and electrical-resistivity measurements can be used to obtain separate lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Failure of the oxygen-vacancy sample to exhibit lower lattice thermal conductivity than the unchanged control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The nominal initial material contains no oxygen, while the intervention presupposes an oxygen-bearing reference population from which oxygen vacancies can be created. No prior oxygen incorporation, oxygen site occupancy, or vacancy definition is specified, making the modified state internally underdefined relative to the unchanged baseline.
